AlternateTargets: a bronze head and iron brow
Senses.Explanation: Literally, “bronze-headed and iron-browed.” Chan texts use the compact bodily description as an epithet for unusually formidable people, especially monks imagined as able to withstand severe encounter. One hall address places “bronze-headed and iron-browed” directly under “the patch-robed monk's gate.” Verses nevertheless say that even such a fellow receives a welt from one staff-blow, or stands bloodied under the staff's command. Elsewhere the phrase itself answers “What is buddha?”, followed by the equally concrete “bird's beak and fish's gills.” These occurrences establish the epithet and its Chan setting; they do not establish literal metal anatomy or an occult quality. The headword occurs 208 times across 114 allowlisted texts.
Senses.Note: Adjectival and substantivized uses refer to the same kind of formidable person and do not require separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 十地心驚，二乘罔測，衲僧門下，銅頭鐵額
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jianzhong Jingguo Continuation of the Lamp Record (建中靖國續燈錄): the explicit Dayu Shouzhi heading governs the hall address; Dayu Shouzhi says that the ten stages are startled and the two vehicles cannot measure, while beneath the patch-robed gate there are copper heads and iron foreheads.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是佛？師云：銅頭鐵額。僧曰：意旨如何？師云：鳥觜魚腮
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jianzhong Jingguo Continuation of the Lamp Record (建中靖國續燈錄): inside Langya Huijue's explicitly headed section, Langya Huijue answers 'what is Buddha?' with 'copper head and iron forehead' and explains with 'bird beak and fish gills.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 縱使銅頭鐵額漢，也須一棒一條痕
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): in the nun Fajing Hao's explicitly headed section, Fajing Hao says that even a fellow with a copper head and iron brow must receive one welt from each staff-blow.

Occurrences.Kwic: 銅頭鐵額漢，盡在此山中
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Lianfeng (蓮峰禪師語錄): in his Xinghua Ximing Monastery verse, Lianfeng says bronze-headed, iron-browed fellows are all within this mountain.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一棒施行該百令，銅頭鐵額血淋身
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jie Weizhou (介為舟禪師語錄): entering his room for a private interview session, Jie Weizhou says that one enacted staff-blow encompasses a hundred commands and leaves copper heads and iron foreheads streaming blood.
